# Scenarios for the fake codex app-server

`test/fake-codex/fake-codex.mjs` answers CodeRay's requests itself (initialize, account/read, model/list (in two pages), skills/list, config/read, thread/start, thread/resume, turn/start, turn/steer (an error when no turn runs or `expectedTurnId` names another), turn/interrupt, account/login/start, account/login/cancel, account/logout) and replays one of these files during turns. Shapes are trimmed from the recorded transcripts of codex-cli 0.160.0 in `recorded/` (sanitized copies of the 2026-10-13 verification runs; `docs/spike/2026-10-13-codex-verified.md`). Every line is one of:

| Line | Effect |
|---|---|
| `{"method": …, "params": …}` | A notification, sent as is. |
| `{"request": "<method>", "params": …}` | A server request with a fresh numeric id; the fake waits for the reply, records it as `{ reply: { method, result } }` (an error reply as `result: { error }`), sends `serverRequest/resolved` and keeps its `decision` or `action` for `when`. A reply to a request no longer waited for is recorded with `method: null`. An interrupt stops the wait with no reply recorded, and `serverRequest/resolved` follows the turn's `turn/completed` (the order 0.160.0 uses: `recorded/p03-gate-patchAccept.jsonl`, `recorded/p03-gate-patchNoAnswer.jsonl`). With `"withdrawMs": N` the fake stops waiting after N ms on its own, sends `serverRequest/resolved` and goes on. With `"meanwhile": [{ "method", "params" }, …]` it sends those notifications right after the request, while it waits. |
| `{"fake": "await-turn"}` | Ends this turn's lines: the fake sends `turn/completed` (`completed`, or `interrupted` after `turn/interrupt`) and plays the next lines at the next `turn/start`. Lines before the first `await-turn` play during the first turn. A fake started again with the same `FAKE_CODEX_RECORD` (a Stop restarts the app-server) goes on from the line the previous one reached. |
| `{"fake": "sleep", "ms": N}` | Waits; an interrupt ends the wait. |
| `{"fake": "write", "path", "content"}` | Writes a file under the thread's `cwd` (stands for a patch or command that ran). |
| `{"fake": "spawn-sleeper"}` | Starts a `sleep 600` child in a process group of its own (as codex starts a shell command), records `{ sleeperPid }`; SIGTERM of the fake kills it (as the real app-server's SIGTERM ends its shell commands). |
| `{"fake": "fail", "message", "codexErrorInfo"?}` | Ends the turn `failed` with that error (and its `codexErrorInfo`, default `null`). |
| `{"fake": "exit", "code": N}` | Exits with code N. |
| `"when": "accept"\|"decline"` | The line plays only if the last reply's `decision` or `action` was that. |

`$THREAD`, `$TURN` and `$CWD` are replaced by the thread id, the turn id and the thread's working directory. Environment: `FAKE_CODEX_SCENARIO` (this file), `FAKE_CODEX_RECORD` (one JSON line per start and per client message: `{ pid, argv, codexHome, credentials, secrets }`, `{ in: { method, params } }`), `FAKE_CODEX_VERSION` (default `0.160.0`), `FAKE_CODEX_ACCOUNT=none` (signed out), `FAKE_CODEX_ECHO_SANDBOX=workspace-write` (a wrong policy echo), `FAKE_CODEX_ECHO` (JSON merged into the echo of `thread/start` and `thread/resume`), `FAKE_CODEX_SLOW` (a method the fake answers late: `FAKE_CODEX_SLOW_MS`, default 300 ms), `FAKE_CODEX_CRASH` (a method on which the fake exits with an error line), `FAKE_CODEX_SILENT` (a method the fake never answers), `FAKE_CODEX_TURN_STARTED_MS` (how long after its `turn/start` answer the turn starts), `FAKE_CODEX_TURN_REPLY=late` (`turn/start` answered only after its turn ended), `FAKE_CODEX_USER_AGENT` (the `userAgent` of `initialize`), `FAKE_CODEX_RESUME_ERROR` (the error every `thread/resume` gets, `$THREAD` its thread id: 0.160.0 answers `no rollout found for thread id $THREAD` for a thread that never ran a turn), `FAKE_CODEX_USER_SERVERS` (JSON of the user's `mcp_servers`, default `{"node_repl":{"command":"node"}}`), `FAKE_CODEX_CONFIG` (JSON of the rest of the user's configuration `config/read` returns), `FAKE_CODEX_EXTRA_SERVER` (a server that starts although nobody configured it), `FAKE_CODEX_LOGIN` (`ok`, `fail`, `hang`, `silent`: the account is stored without `account/login/completed`), `FAKE_CODEX_LOGIN_ERROR` (the error of a `fail`ed sign-in), `FAKE_CODEX_AUTH_URL` (the browser sign-in's page), `FAKE_CODEX_EMAIL`. Under `CODEX_HOME` the account is `auth.json` in it, which a login writes and a logout removes, and a cancelled sign-in writes `.tmp/` into it 100 ms later, as codex does even after its home was removed; without `CODEX_HOME` the fake is a signed-in System account and refuses to sign in or out.

The fake answers a request only after the handshake the verification runs used (`initialize`, then the `initialized` notification). Like 0.160.0, the fake refuses a `thread/start` or `thread/resume` whose config switches off a server nobody defines. The fake exits when its stdin closes, as 0.160.0 does (`docs/spike/2026-10-16-codex-engine-smoke.md`).
